chapter: Armstrong, Parker and life inside the Basie band
title: Kids humming the solos at the Earle Theater in Philadelphia
summary: Fans knew the Basie records note for note, and noticed when Tate played a different solo on Rockabye, Basie.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: What was the incident that happened in Philadelphia with the Basie band? Pittsburgh?
Pittsburgh?
You were going to tell me some incident in the Basie band.
Pittsburgh? Did I say -- did I mention it yesterday?
Yeah.
Let me see. What --
I think it had to do with your taking over from Herschel or --
Oh, --
Solos?
Oh, yeah, oh, yeah. Oh, I think what you remember -- what I meant was like during those days, kids remembered those solos.
Uh-huh.
I think that's what we were started to talk --
Yeah.
And they -- you know, like they knew them, note for note, and when you played a song, you know, they would

hum the solos. That's why Basie wanted me to play Herschel's solos, because they knew the solo, everybody's solo. So I remember when we made "Rockabye, Basie." Well, I used to play it and we stretched it because Basie had me to play like four, five more choruses, because I featured on "Rockabye, Basie." I'd play that and play some more things.

So sometimes I -- one day in Philadelphia at the Earle Theater of the front theater was just loaded with kids, just -- and they were humming and humming the riffs and things with us. So I didn't play that regular solo that I recorded.
(Laughter.)

And when we come backstage, they wanted your autograph and everything, so they asked me, they says, "You know what? We thought you were the one that made that 'Rockabye, Basie.'" I said, "Well, I did." They says, "Well, you didn't play that solo. That wasn't the solo you recorded."
(Laughter.)
Because they say, "We know it." And they hummed the solo to me, you know, like the record. And I think that's what I meant.
Yes, right.
This was in Philadelphia. And they knew them all. They knew Prez' solos, they knew the trumpet solo, trombone solos, everything. And of course, everybody had their
own thing and it was a variety of styles in those days.
